text:
sanjay: Quick RFC follow-up on paged/blocked KV cache + attention kernel compatibility. Need to settle API boundaries, eviction semantics, and fragmentation handling before we ship the kernel-selection changes. TL;DR: propose small kernel ABI + capability flags, a staging/gather helper for contiguous-only kernels, and an eviction contract.

alex: +1. Question: what exactly does the ABI expose? Can kernels request pages synchronously, or do we force async page pulls?

sanjay: goal is to support both. Kernels can declare capabilities: `supports_contiguous_kv`, `supports_paged_kv`, `max_page_size`. Runtime will present either a paged view (page callbacks) or a contiguous staging buffer if kernel asks for contiguous. Paging ops should be async to avoid stalling GPU, but we may allow a blocking helper for simple kernels.

alex: I worry about overhead for fused attention kernels that expect contiguous KV. A staging/gather helper would help, but copying per step kills perf. Idea: `gather_view` that pins pages into a preallocated GPU staging buffer and returns a lightweight pointer for the kernel to use for the forward. Pseudocode: \n```\nstaging = runtime.alloc_staging(batch * window)\nawait page_loader.fill_async(staging, page_ids)\nkernel.forward_with_gather(staging)\n```\nThis keeps kernel code unchanged mostly.

maria: eviction concerns: naive LRU on pages leads to heavy fragmentation if page sizes vary or if we use block allocation. We should standardize on fixed-size blocks (power-of-two) to make coalescing easier. Propose `block_size = 64 tokens` as default and allow model-level override.

elaine: agree on fixed blocks. Also propose a low-priority background compaction/defrag task that runs during idle windows. That avoids long pauses doing big compacts.

maria: also want to consider a generational eviction policy: keep a small hot set pinned (recently used or high-score) and evict from cold set. We can keep per-page hotness counters and surface them to the console.

alex: what about fragmentation inside pages when kernels write variable-length KV? Do we support in-place partial updates or always rewrite whole block?

sanjay: prefer immutable pages: writes create new page versions to simplify concurrency and avoid in-place fragmentation. Then GC can reclaim old versions during compaction. Immutable pages + block allocation simplifies correctness.

elaine: that means more memory churn, but GC/compaction plus a good eviction policy should balance it. We should expose a metric `kv_page_reuse_ratio` and `kv_fragmentation_pct` so we can tune.

sanjay: fallback story: if kernel cannot work with paged view and staging isn't fast enough, runtime will route that workload to nodes with contiguous-memory allocation (dedicated pool) or fall back to slower CPU-based gather. Need a policy flag `contiguous_required` on route config.

alex: sounds reasonable. For prototype I'll implement `gather_view` + async page_loader API. I'll include an opt-in fast-path that pins pages on GPU via CUDA IPC where supported.

maria: i'll run microbenchmarks comparing LRU vs generational (with fixed block_size 64/128) on typical convo workloads. Will instrument fragmentation metrics.

elaine: i'll add defrag worker + console charts. Also add alert if `kv_fragmentation_pct > 30%` for >5m.

runtime-bot: prototype shim branch `runtimes/paged-kv-shim` pushed — CI passed on small models. :party_parrot: 

sanjay: Decisions/next steps: 1) define kernel ABI docs (cap flags + async page_loader + staging/gather helper) 2) adopt fixed block allocation (default 64 tokens) + immutable pages 3) eviction = generational with small pinned hot set; metrics required 4) background compaction task + alerts.

sanjay: Action owners: alex -> prototype gather_view + GPU pin fast-path; maria -> perf matrix + eviction experiments; elaine -> defrag worker + metrics/alerts. I'll draft the formal follow-up RFC update and push to the RFC thread with ABI sketches.

alex: ack, starting prototype.

maria: ack, will share benchmark plan tomorrow.

elaine: ack, will add dashboard widgets this week.

sanjay: thanks all, we'll reconvene after initial numbers. :thumbsup:
